summary: Catherine Bell was a scholar of religious studies and sinology who studied under Joseph Mitsuo Kitagawa at the University of Chicago (~1976–1983). She served as the Bernard J. Hanley Professor of Religious Studies at Santa Clara University from 1985 to 2008.

Catherine Elaine Prueitt specializes in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. She earned a BA from the University of Rochester in 2007 and a PhD from Emory University in 2016, studying under Laurie L. Patton and doctoral supervisor John D. Dunne.

Catherine Ludvik works in religious studies, Japanology, and Indology. She completed her PhD at the University of Toronto (2001) under David Waterhouse, Werner Knobl, Yuko Matsuda, and Antonino Forte, and held posts at Hanazono University and the Italian School of East Asian Studies.
Cathy Cantwell specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from the University of Kent (~1984–1989) and held a post at the University of Oxford in 2002.

Cecil Bendall was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Oxford and Cambridge under Edward Byles Cowell and Theodor Benfey. He held posts at the British Museum/Library, UCL/University of London, and served as Professor of Sanskrit at Cambridge.

Cecil Y. Lang studied at Duke University (~1937–1941) and later held academic posts at Yale University (~1949–1957) and the University of Chicago (~1967–1970). From ~1970 to 1991, he served as Professor of English at the University of Virginia.
Chagdud Tulku Rinpoche was a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Delog Dawa Drolma, Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, and Dudjom Rinpoche, and later taught Albion Moonlight Butters.

Chaisit Suwanvarangkul, a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy, conducted research at Kyoto University and the University of Delhi. He was attested as Lecturer in Buddhist Studies at the University of Otago in 2015.

Chakravarthi Ram-Prasad works in philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. After earning a doctorate in philosophy from Oxford, he held research fellowships at Clare Hall, Cambridge, and Trinity College, Oxford, taught at NUS, and became a professor at Lancaster University.

Chamnong Adivadhanasit, working in religious and Buddhist studies, earned a BA from Chulalongkorn University. In 2012, he was attested as a professor at Kasetsart University's Faculty of Social Science and a part-time instructor at Chulalongkorn University.
Champa Thupten Zongtse was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who held posts at the University of Göttingen, where he was attested in 1991 and served as a lecturer in 2009.

Chandrabhal Tripathi was an Indologist who earned his PhD under Ernst Waldschmidt at the University of Göttingen (~1957–1960). He held posts at Göttingen, Cologne, Humboldt University, and served as Professor of Indology at the Free University of Berlin (~1978–1994).

Chang-geun Hwang is a scholar of Buddhist studies who completed a PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 2000. During his studies, he was guided by Morten Schlütter, Minoru Kiyota, and Geshe Lhundub Sopa.

Changhwan Park works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at Otani University and earned a PhD from UC Berkeley under Alexander von Rospatt and Noritoshi Aramaki, later serving as a professor at Geumgang University (attested 2013–2017).

Chanju Mun is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (2001–2002) and completed a PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under supervisors Charles Hallisey, Masahiro Shimoda, Morten Schlütter, Gudrun Bühnemann, and John D. Dunne.

Charlene Elizabeth Makley, a Tibetologist and anthropologist, earned her PhD in 1999 from the University of Michigan, studying under Norma Diamond and Roy Rappaport. She went on to become an associate professor of anthropology at Reed College.

Charles A. Moore was a philosopher who studied at Yale University (~1926–1932). He served as a professor at the University of Hawaii from ~1936 to 1967 and edited Philosophy East and West from ~1951 to 1967.

Charles B. Jones is a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. He completed his PhD under Paul Groner at the University of Virginia (1996) and became an associate professor and associate dean at Catholic University of America.

Charles D. Orzech works in religious studies, sinology, and Buddhist studies. He completed his dissertation at the University of Chicago, chaired the Religious Studies Department at UNC Greensboro (attested 1998–2006), and was a fellow at the National Humanities Center (2009–2010).

Charles Duroiselle worked in archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He held posts at the University of Yangon (~1906–1919), EFEO (~1904–1951), the Archaeological Survey of India (Burma Circle Superintendent, 1919 and 1936), and the Department of Archaeology (1936).
